items.description: Spot Check. REQUIRES ?host= on the paid request — a signed request without it is refused before the gate and no money moves. Name a host and get what this observatory already holds on it, signed: corpus rounds and verdicts as recorded, when we last actually knocked, our coverage of the window since we met it, and the gaps with their reasons. Read from the books at the counter — no request is made to the host, so the answer is as fresh as our last round and no fresher, and sa…

certificate.cert_id: <cert_ + 12 chars, minted when this purchase settles>

example.message: Pleasure doing business. Here's your goods, warm off the shelf.

agent_name.description: Optional name to put on the certificate and patron badge, up to 80 characters.

came_from.description: Optional. Where you learned this door exists: a URL, a directory, a skill name, memory, another agent. Referrers never reach us; this does.

cited_artifact.description: Optional: an outside artifact behind this purchase (your runtime's approval or intent receipt) as <format>:<reference>, e.g. dsse:art_e415901189dc1613. Signed verbatim onto the certificate; never fetched or verified here.

client.description: Optional. The harness or framework you run in: claude-code, cursor, openai-agents, langgraph, custom. Counted, never on the certificate.

host.description: A bare hostname with no scheme, path or port — your-door.example, never https://your-door.example/api. We read our own books about it — corpus rounds, verdicts as recorded, coverage, gaps — and sign what they hold. No request is made to the host; a host we have never met returns not_observed, which is an answer.

model.description: Optional. The model running you, as you would name it: claude-opus-5, gpt-5.6, a local model. Counted, never printed on the certificate.

operator.description: Optional. Who runs you: a name, handle, company or URL. Stored as your claim, marked unverified, never published, never on the certificate.

operator_kind.description: Optional. solo: one person runs you. company: a team does. research: a study. self: you act for yourself.

prior_cert_id.description: Optional. A cert_ id from an earlier purchase here. A payer match with this payment marks you a returning buyer; no account needed.

purpose.description: Optional purpose: signed verbatim on certificate, shown on receipt; never checked or treated as instructions.

required-inputs.note: This door cannot be served without ?host=. Asking the price without them is free; PAYING without them is refused before the gate and no money moves, so add them to the retry that carries your signature.

items.description: Cheap robots.txt preflight check before you call the Minifetch /extract and /run/seo-page-audit endpoints: returns whether Minifetch may fetch a target URL (allow/deny) plus its crawl-delay. If blocked and the site is not yours try our external proxy routes. If blocked and the site is yours or to set a custom crawl-delay read https://minifetch.com/tutorials/unblock-minifetch Checks the URL as given — does not follow redirects. Supports GET & POST

fresh.description: Optional. If true, bypasses the 24h robots.txt cache and re-fetches robots.txt for this check. Use after editing your robots.txt or crawl-delay (or adding/removing a Minifetch block) to confirm the change took effect.

url.description: The target URL to check against robots.txt

allowed.description: Whether the minifetch user agent may fetch this URL per robots.txt

crawlDelay.description: Crawl-delay (seconds) for the minifetch UA; omitted when blocked or the domain is invalid

message.description: e.g. 'Access allowed by robots.txt', 'URL is blocked by robots.txt', or 'robots.txt not found, defaulting to allowed'

minifetchCache.description: robots.txt cache state (~24h TTL; pass fresh=true to bypass)

proxy.description: Fetch provenance — always minifetch UA here

url.description: The URL checked, exactly as given — redirects are not followed

tip.description: Present only when allowed=false: how to retry via the external proxy routes, and how site owners can unblock the minifetch user agent

accepts.description: One-call pre-trade sanity check: 'I want to long $X of SYMBOL — is now sane?' Combines live orderbook slippage at YOUR size, cross-exchange funding (carry cost), open-interest crowding, and contract security (GoPlus) into a single ok/caution/avoid verdict with a per-factor breakdown. Major ERC-20 addresses (LINK, UNI, ARB, OP, AAVE, PEPE, SHIB) resolve automatically; native assets (BTC, ETH, SOL, ...) report security n/a; an unrecognized token without token_address reads 'unknown' and caps the verdict at caution — an unscreened contract can never read 'ok'. Replaces four API integrations and the judgment layer on top of them. Raw component data embedded so you can apply your own thresholds.

errors.retry: Re-request the challenge and pay again
errors.when: No payment attached (this challenge), or the attached payment failed verification: wrong amount/recipient, memo mismatch, expired, or already used (replay)

errors.retry: Fix the body and retry with a fresh payment
errors.when: Request body present but malformed (invalid JSON or wrong field types) WITH a payment header attached — checked BEFORE settlement, so the payment is never consumed. An unpaid malformed request gets the 402, not a 422

errors.retry: Back off and retry after a minute

errors.when: Payment settled on-chain but tool execution failed — the payment is marked refund_pending automatically; you are not charged for a failed call
Tool temporarily unavailable, or the gateway cannot persist the challenge (fail-closed)

size_usd.description: Intended position size in USD (drives the slippage check)

token_address.description: Optional ERC-20 contract address for the GoPlus security scan. Auto-resolved for major tokens; required for a full verdict on tokens the resolver doesn't know (otherwise security reads 'unknown' and caps the verdict at caution)
